description:
FILED s536h (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while fixing #4263.  PRE-EXISTING (base ba7863a3 identical).  SILENT (output goes to a file perl never creates).

    chdir "/tmp/x"; open(my $o, ">-:raw") or die; print fileno($o), "\n"; print "file? ", (-e "-:raw" ? 1 : 0), "\n";
  perl 5.40.3: 1 / file? 0        PCL: 5 / file? 1   (a file "-:raw" is created)

perl doio.c (the 2-arg '>' and '<' branches): `if (*type == IoTYPE_STD && (!type[1] || isSPACE(type[1]) || type[1] == ':'))` -> fp = PerlIO_stdout() / PerlIO_stdin(), IoTYPE_STD, and the layers after the `:` apply to THAT PerlIO (i.e. to the standard stream itself).  PCL's %p-open-parse-2arg leaves "-:raw" as the file name, and %p-open-impl's `-` arm (s536h: an %p-fdopen-alias with STD) matches the exact name "-" only.  Fix shape: in the 2-arg parse, a name "-" followed by `:LAYERS` is the STD handle with those layers (binmode of the standard stream) -- probe what `binmode` of an alias does to STDOUT's own layer first.  Probe: scratch/s536h/p/m1b.pl (row a4) in the s536h worktree.
subject: 2-arg `open(F, ">-:raw")` (a `-` followed by a layer) opens a FILE named "-:raw" in PCL; perl opens STDOUT and applies the layer (doio.c: `-` followed by NUL, space or `:` is IoTYPE_STD)
